name: Parsonage-Turner Syndrome / Neuralgic Amyotrophy
definition: Acute immune-mediated brachial neuritis characterized by severe shoulder/arm pain followed by patchy weakness and muscle wasting.

investigations.principle: Electrodiagnostics support diagnosis; MRI is used to exclude structural lesions and may show denervation.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Recovery can take months to years; persistent focal deficits may require nerve specialist review.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa/Vata-neuralgic phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Acute immune-mediated brachial neuritis characterized by severe shoulder/arm pain followed by patchy weakness and muscle wasting.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
